messages.subject: just pushed remaining slicing functions + Eigen traits
parts:
I just pushed a big block of commits. Almost all of it
revolves around matrix and array slicing. We already
had block(). I added tests for Marcus's sub_row() and sub_col()
and pulled them into their own file. I also added
vector, row vector and array head() and tail() and segment()
functions. I cleaned up the print spacing in some of the
error handling. Everything's tested, documented and added to
function signatures. Doing this all the "right way" is really
really time consuming --- I don't know how Daniel Lee rips through
this stuff so quickly.

I still haven't produced model files to compile with all the
usages.

I added a validate_std_vector_index in math/matrix, but it should
probably go somewhere else. I just didn't see a natural place
for it. I followed the other index error functions in requiring
the adjustment for indexing by 1 on the outside.

Our library is a bit awkward in how it's set up because of
the indexing from 1 in Stan and indexing from 0 in C++.
Our functions typically follow the Stan indexing from 1, but the
underlying std::vector and Matrix objects use indexing from 0.

I also pushed a slight change to the Eigen numerical traits
that would've leaked memory had we continually printed agrad
matrices. We were returning new agrad::var objects in print.
I realized this from a question on the Eigen list
by Bradley Bell, who's working on adding Eigen to CppAD, another
open-source C++ auto-diff package (I responded on the Eigen
list).

I also applied some patches to the doc and added some
more acknowledgments.

- Bob
